claims.claim: charging a lithium-ion phone battery always dissipates some power as heat
claims.definition: waste heat produced by electrical resistance in the cable, charge circuitry, and cell internals during charging
claims.measured_value: on the order of a few percent of charging power; rises with charge rate
claims.authoritative_source: Battery University BU-808; OEM thermal-management documentation
claims.notes: direction is certain; exact percentage varies by device and charge rate, so narration stays qualitative

claims.claim: charging stores energy by moving lithium ions between electrodes
claims.definition: lithium ions intercalate from cathode to anode while charging; they return during discharge

claims.claim: phones reduce charging current when the battery runs hot (thermal throttling)
claims.definition: charge controllers taper current above battery-temperature thresholds to protect cell life
claims.measured_value: taper begins above roughly 35-45 C cell temperature, device dependent
claims.authoritative_source: Apple maximizing battery performance; Android charge-health documentation
